prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: cancelling cover to save money. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member says they want to cancel cover to save money, I check whether they still need the policy for a mortgage condition, a financed vehicle, or any open claim before I do anything else."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a cancellation request comes after a loss is reported, I treat the claim and the cover separately, because cancelling mid-process does not remove our duty to assess the already-notified event fairly."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the main issue is affordability, I look for a simpler fix first, such as reducing optional extras or adjusting the excess, rather than assuming cancellation is the only route."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a member is cancelling because they have found cheaper cover, I prefer to confirm the exact start date of the new policy so there is no gap in cover for home or motor risks."},{"type":"fact","content":"When there is a direct debit schedule in place, I check whether any instalments, fees, or returned-payment charges will still be due after cancellation, because those can affect the final outcome."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member sounds unsure, I slow the conversation down and explain the difference between cancelling at renewal and cancelling mid-term, since those can lead to very different costs."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a motor policy is being cancelled, I like to remind the member to stop using the vehicle only if they have no other valid insurance in place, because driving uninsured creates avoidable risk."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a home policy is being cancelled, I check whether the property is still occupied, empty, let, or in the middle of sale or completion, because the required cover can change with the situation."},{"type":"observation","content":"When savings are the driver, I often find the best next step is to review cover levels at renewal rather than cancel immediately, especially where the member has not compared the real value of the protections."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I sense cancellation is being used as a pressure point, I prefer to offer a clear summary of what would be lost, what would still be payable, and what alternatives exist, so the member can make an informed choice."}]}
